text:
Maya R: Hey all — dropping a concise pack of lane-specific goal & feedback prompts I sketched for managers to use in 1:1s and during self-reviews. Wanted a quick sanity-check before we publish in the handbook. :spiral_note_pad:

Maya R: TL;DR: short prompts for 3 career lanes (IC, Manager, Platform) + a 'what good looks like' line + 1 manager calibration cue. Use as copy-paste in 1:1s or feedback forms.

Maya R: Template preview (super compact):
```
Lane: IC (Senior/Staff)
- OKR line: "Improve inference tail-latency 95th% by 18% while keeping cost per token +/-5%"
- What good looks like: "Consistently hits latency SLO across staged workloads; regression <1% in quality evals"
- Manager cue: "Ask for two specific examples where they designed a tradeoff and the resulting metric changes"

Lane: Manager
- OKR line: "Enable two squads to reduce request P95 by 20% through rollout of shared batching infra"
- What good looks like: "Teams adopt the pattern, metrics show improved SLOs, and incidents drop month-over-month"
- Manager cue: "Probe how they coached engineers through tradeoffs vs doing the technical work themselves"

Lane: Platform/Infra
- OKR line: "Ship autoscaler v2 and reduce GPU idle time by 30% for steady-state workloads"
- What good looks like: "Stable autoscaling in prod for 3 weeks; cost savings observed in billing"
- Manager cue: "Ask which regressions were caught in staging vs production and why"
```

Sam K: Love the lanes. Can we add a one-line prompt for cross-functional impact? e.g., "Who benefitted outside your team?"

Maya R: Good call — adding a cross-impact bullet to each lane. Example: "Cross-impact: Reduced time-to-response for Search team and lowered ops tickets by X"

Elaine (People Ops): Also recommend a 30s micro-script managers can read aloud in 1:1s so it doesn’t sound canned. Draft:
"I want to focus today on one or two examples where you made measurable impact and one area you'd like help leveling up — let's pick a tangible next step."

Nina L (Eng Manager): Tiny nit: for IC 'what good looks like' maybe include a measurable frequency (e.g., ">=3 evals pass" or "<1% regressions per month") so it's reviewable.

Maya R: yup — will add bracketed metrics. Final tweak: include an optional 'evidence artifacts' line to paste into reviews (PR links, eval IDs, rollout notes).

hr-bot: Resource posted: https://handbook.redwood.company/people-ops/goal-cards — public draft updated.

Sam K: Quick question — should managers be required to collect at least one peer quote for every manager-level self-review?

Elaine (People Ops): Not required, recommended. We'll note: "peer quote encouraged for manager lane; 1 suggested, 2+ ideal". Keeps process lightweight.

Maya R: Plan: incorporate feedback, add cross-impact and evidence lines, publish as "Lane-focused goal & feedback cards" in handbook and add a short header in the review form so managers can paste.

Nina L (Eng Manager): Looks great — will pilot with my ICs this cycle and report back with phrasing that landed.

Maya R: Thanks team — expect a final doc update tomorrow. If anyone wants edits before I push, drop them here. :thumbsup:
